method:
The evaluation uses two strictly independent computational paths to ensure zero data leakage between the VLM prediction and the ground truth.

REFERENCE PATH (bottom row, left to right): A Rule-Based Benchmark Generator produces the Ground-Truth Scene JSON directly, without any VLM involvement. This JSON is converted to the Reference 3D Geometry (the actual room with walls, obstacles, openings as solid surfaces). The reference 3D geometry is independently meshed and solved with OpenFOAM to produce the Reference CFD Solution. Additionally, the Reference 3D Geometry is rendered from multiple camera viewpoints (perspective, bird's-eye, floor plan, wireframe, section) to produce multi-view images. These rendered images serve ONLY as test input stimuli for the VLM. A dashed arrow labeled 'test input only' goes from the Reference 3D Geometry's multi-view rendering output upward to the VLM in the predicted path. The images do NOT participate in the reference CFD computation.

PREDICTED PATH (top row, left to right): The VLM (Gemini) receives the multi-view rendered images as its sole input. It independently extracts a Predicted Scene JSON describing the room geometry, obstacles, and openings. This predicted JSON is converted to a Predicted 3D Geometry (which will generally differ from the reference 3D geometry due to VLM interpretation errors). The predicted 3D geometry is meshed using Gmsh and solved with the same OpenFOAM pipeline to produce the Predicted CFD Solution.

METRIC COMPARISON (right side): Both the Predicted CFD Solution and Reference CFD Solution converge at a Metric Comparison stage, which samples both flow fields onto a common normalised lattice and computes two output scores: Structural Similarity Score (geometric fidelity) and Reference CFD Agreement Score (flow-field accuracy).

CRITICAL VISUAL EMPHASIS: Show both the Predicted 3D Geometry block and Reference 3D Geometry block prominently, making it visually obvious that they are separate objects derived from different JSON sources. The multi-view rendering step originates from the Reference 3D Geometry (not from the JSON directly), reinforcing that the images are views of the reference geometry used only to test the VLM. The VLM never sees the ground-truth JSON or reference 3D geometry data — it only sees the rendered images.
caption: Evaluation pathway with data-leakage prevention. The predicted path (top) processes multi-view rendered images through the VLM to obtain a predicted scene JSON, which is converted to a predicted 3D geometry, meshed, and solved. The reference path (bottom) generates the ground-truth scene JSON via a rule-based generator, converts it to a reference 3D geometry, and solves independently without VLM involvement. Multi-view images rendered from the ground-truth scene serve only as VLM test inputs (dashed arrow) and do not participate in the reference computation. Both paths converge at the metric comparison stage.
